summary: The idea is sound: get rid of cuBLAS's separate splitKreduce step and stream the weight with 64-wide tiles over a full 128-CTA grid. But the spec's BLOCK_K=128 does not match the unpooler kernel it claims to copy (that one used BLOCK_K=256). As written, each CTA keeps the same 64 KB of weight in flight as the 3.3 TB/s pooler kernel, not the 128 KB of the 3.73 TB/s unpooler kernel. Run it with one BLOCK_K=256 control so that a flat result can be read.
justification: Mechanism. Pooler at m<=32 is 67.1 MB of bf16 weight. Today it is nvjet splitK at 18.3-20.2 us plus cublasLt splitKreduce at 1.6-1.9 us, and the shape takes 21.2-22.0 us against a 14.0-14.1 us floor. Removing the second graph node and streaming nearer 3.7 TB/s is plausible on H200. There is direct prior evidence. pooler-triton-skinny-m32 (full-K, BLOCK_N=32, BLOCK_K=256, 4 stages, 128 programs) already measured 20.27-20.51 us at m=1/8/16, paired 1.057-1.063 vs SGLang. So a Triton pooler beats cuBLAS by about 1 us at m<=16 even at 3.3 TB/s. That run came out neutral overall (0.998x) only because decode_32 lost 11% (24.5 us vs 21.9). unpooler-full-triton-skinny-m32 moved the same 67.1 MB in 17.97 us at m=16 (3.73 TB/s, paired 1.033). The direction 'faster at decode_1/verify_1/decode_16' is well supported. The 'target <= 19 us' rests on reproducing the unpooler program. WEAKEST LINK: the claim that 'per-CTA work is therefore exactly the unpooler-full-triton-skinny-m32 program' is false as specified. That kernel used BLOCK_N=64, BLOCK_K=256, num_stages=4: 32 KB of weight per stage, 128 KB of weight in flight, 160 KB of smem at BLOCK_M=16 (UNPOOLER_NUM_STAGES comment in its patch). This hypothesis uses BLOCK_K=128 with 4 stages: 64x128x2 = 16 KB of weight per stage and 64 KB in flight. That is byte-for-byte the in-flight depth of the 3.3 TB/s pooler kernel (32x256x2 = 16 KB/stage, 64 KB in flight, per POOLER_NUM_STAGES). The only measured difference between the 3.3 and 3.73 TB/s configs that the family has is the tile and stage bytes, not split-K. So this spec may land at about 20.3 us, the old pooler's rate, and fail to tell 'split-K + BLOCK_N=64 does not help' apart from 'stage depth was the limit'. Secondary: decode_32 marked flat is optimistic. Both earlier Triton m=32 pooler rows lost 11% (24.5-24.6 us). The unpooler m=32 rows lost 3-9% (19.27 us with BLOCK_M=32, 20.8 us with the BLOCK_M=16 control). Split-K 2 halves per-CTA K, so per-CTA x re-read drops from the old pooler's 512 KB to 256 KB (32 MB from L2 in total, the same as the unpooler m=32 case). That makes the unpooler's 19.3 us, about a 3% loss, the right prior, not flat. A loss there is about 30% of the decode_32 load and could erase one shape's gain in the geomean. Expected magnitudes are consistent with TASK.md: equal weights of 62, pooler is 31-32% of each of the four loads, and about 2 us per shape gives about +3% on each of three loads. Verify_16/32 (m=128/256) and router are proper in-run controls. Semaphore design: deterministic, because the fixed 0..SPLIT_K-1 order is applied by whichever CTA arrives last. It is capture-safe if the counter is zero at capture and every replay completes, which the self-reset by atomic_xchg and the re-zero after warm-up provide. Ordering: store partials, bar.sync (tl.debug_barrier), then a gpu-scope acq_rel scalar atomic. This relies on the barrier making the other threads' stores cumulative with thread 0's release. That is accepted practice, but a fence on the release side (CUTLASS Semaphore uses __threadfence before the atomic) is cheap insurance. On the acquire side, the other threads in the last CTA must be ordered after thread 0's acquire. Triton's broadcast of the scalar result through smem normally inserts a barrier. The implementer should confirm this in the TTGIR/PTX or add tl.debug_barrier() after the ticket. The .cg reloads of the partials are correct, since L1 is not coherent.
confounders: router-triton-hilo-fused-control-splitk-all-m (master's 1.151x): different layer, its own CUDA graph per shape, cold L2 per replay, no shared workspace or counters. It cannot move the pooler rows. The router rows are a reproducibility control only. The headline will be judged against 1.151x, so read the gain from the per-shape pooler rows and paired ratios, not from the headline delta.

sglang-gemm-dispatch-parity: defines the cuBLAS path being replaced, and keeps pooler m>=128 and all other layers unchanged. This is not an interaction: verify_16/verify_32 pooler rows stay on it and serve as in-run flat controls.
router-hilo-at-m8: router-only threshold, now subsumed by the Triton router. No shared path with the pooler. Not a confounder.
interference: No landed hypothesis touches the pooler path, the pooler's memory traffic or its numerics, so ab-revert and ab-tune are not warranted. A gain at m<=16 would be attributable to the change on its own. The ambiguity is internal. The hypothesis says it reproduces the 3.73 TB/s unpooler program, but its BLOCK_K=128 / 4-stage pipeline holds the 64 KB in-flight depth of the 3.3 TB/s pooler program. Suppose the parent comes back about 20.3 us at m=1/8/16 (no better than pooler-triton-skinny-m32) or loses at decode_32. Then you cannot tell whether split-K + BLOCK_N=64 + in-kernel reduce fails, or whether only the stage bytes held it back. A modest gain (about 20 us) would also be indistinguishable from the old full-K kernel's gain. One control fixes this: set BLOCK_K=256 (16 K-steps per 4096 slice) with num_stages=4, which is the unpooler's per-CTA tile, stage depth and step count exactly, with everything else identical. Compare the two runs per row (kernel us at m=1/8/16 and at m=32). That separates the effect of stage depth from that of the split-K/semaphore design, and tells you which variant to promote. A BLOCK_M=16-two-accumulator variant at m=32 is not worth a parallel run: the unpooler control already showed it does not fix m=32 (20.8 us vs 19.3). If decode_32 regresses, the next follow-up is to route only m<=16, not to run another m=32 tile experiment.
rules_flags: None blocking. Workspace pooler_ws and counter pooler_cnt are scratch, made in prepare() from shapes only, and fully overwritten or reset each call. Nothing input-derived survives between calls. Keep it that way: do not skip the counter reset on any path.

Graph safety: the counter must be zero when capture happens and after every eager call (tests, warm-up). The self-reset handles this on success. Re-zero after warm-up as specified. If any eager launch could exit early (for example, a masked or empty tile), make sure every CTA still increments its ticket, or the counter is left nonzero and every later replay gives wrong output.

Precision: fp32 accumulate and a single bf16 rounding of the two-partial sum. This meets the weights-at-own-precision rule and the bf16 output dtype, and matches cuBLAS splitK numerics. The m=7 pooler test exercises masked rows.
No host syncs, no value-dependent branching: BLOCK_M is chosen from the shape (m) only. Allocating out with torch.empty inside the graph is fine.

companions.change: From the parent's branch (pooler-triton-splitk2-blockn64-semaphore), change exactly one constant: the pooler split-K kernel's BLOCK_K from 128 to 256, so each CTA's K-slice of 4096 is 16 K-steps instead of 32. Keep num_stages=4, num_warps=4, BLOCK_N=64, SPLIT_K=2, grid (64, 2) = 128 CTAs, BLOCK_M=16 for m<=16 and 32 for 17..32. Keep the direct transposed weight addressing, the fp32 workspace, the barrier + acq_rel ticket + last-CTA fixed-order reduce and atomic_xchg reset, the routing (pooler m<=32 only), and the warm-up plus re-zero in prepare(). Smem becomes 4 x (64x256 + BLOCK_M x256) x 2 B = 160 KB at BLOCK_M=16 and 192 KB at BLOCK_M=32. This is exactly the unpooler-full-triton-skinny-m32 per-CTA program, and it fits H200's 227 KB. If Triton rejects 192 KB at BLOCK_M=32, use num_stages=3 for the BLOCK_M=32 specialization only and record that.

expected.why: 128 KB of weight in flight per CTA, the 3.73 TB/s unpooler config. Expect about 18-18.5 us plus the reduce tail, below the parent if the parent is stage-bound at about 20.3 us
the exact m=16 unpooler program that measured 17.97 us on the same 67.1 MB
unpooler BLOCK_M=32 at this tile measured 19.27 us (paired 0.973); expect about 20 us vs nvjet's 20.2+1.9, roughly flat to slightly faster

companions.reason: Separates stage depth (64 KB vs 128 KB of weight in flight per CTA, the only measured difference between the 3.3 and 3.73 TB/s Triton configs) from the parent's own design (split-K 2 + BLOCK_N=64 + semaphore reduce). Parent about 20.3 us and control about 18.5 us: the parent's spec, not its design, was at fault, and the control is the one to promote. Both about 20.3 us: split-K/semaphore costs as much as it saves. Both about 18.5 us: BLOCK_N=64 + split-K is what matters.

open_questions: Does Triton emit a barrier between the scalar atomic's result broadcast and the other threads' .cg reloads in the last CTA? If not, add tl.debug_barrier() after the ticket. Also consider a release-side fence before the atomic, as CUTLASS Semaphore does.
Is the ws store masked to rows < m? At m=1 an unmasked BLOCK_M=16 store writes 16x more partial bytes than needed. This is harmless (about 128 KB total) but adds to the reduce tail.

decode_32: given both earlier Triton m=32 pooler rows lost 11% and the unpooler m=32 rows lost 3-9%, should the promotable variant route only m<=16 (leaving decode_32 on cuBLAS) if decode_32 regresses? Per-shape rows from this run answer that without another companion.

Readout should use the Triton kernel's own us per row (top_kernels) and the paired ratios, calibrated against pooler-triton-skinny-m32's 20.27-20.51 us rows at m=1/8/16. Headline deltas vs 1.151x will be inside the CI (expected about +2-3% geomean).
